front.title: Provider Authentication for More Instant Messaging Interoperability (MIMI)

abstract.t: The MIMI protocol requires each provider to authenticate the provider that sends it a request. It specifies mutually authenticated TLS for this, but not where the client certificates come from or which trust anchors check them. The public Web PKI has stopped issuing such certificates. This document defines how MIMI providers authenticate each other without it. The mechanism every provider implements is a key published in DNS under the provider's domain, used to sign each request with HTTP Message Signatures. DANE client certificates, client certificates from configured PKIX trust anchors, and locally configured trust lists are defined as additional mechanisms that a provider can accept by local policy.
